segments.start_exact: There was once a poor widow who lived in a lonely cottage.
segments.end_exact:
behind them upon a perch sat a white dove with its head hidden beneath its
      wings.
segments.summary: Introduces the widow and her daughters Snow-white and Rose-red, their gentle natures, their forest wanderings, angelic protection, and daily household life.
segments.reason: Expository introduction unified by the cottage/forest setting and family; describes habitual life without a focused goal-conflict-outcome structure, so narrative_scene.

segments.start_exact:
One evening, as they were thus sitting comfortably together, someone
      knocked at the door
segments.end_exact:
the doors were never fastened
      until their black friend had arrived.
segments.summary: A bear knocks and is welcomed at the cottage; the children play with him, he stays by the hearth nightly through winter.
segments.reason: Unified by the cottage setting and the recurring evening visits; the initial fright resolves quickly into a friendly habitual arrangement, lacking sustained conflict/outcome structure, so narrative_scene.

segments.start_exact: When spring had come and all outside was green, the bear said one morning
segments.end_exact:
The
      bear ran away quickly, and was soon out of sight behind the trees.
segments.summary: In spring the bear announces he must leave to guard treasures from dwarfs; departing, his coat tears revealing a glint of gold.
segments.reason: Distinct time shift (spring) and departure event, unified by cottage doorway; descriptive/transitional without goal-conflict-outcome, so narrative_scene.

segments.start_exact:
A short time afterwards the mother sent her children into the forest to
      get firewood.
segments.end_exact:
went
      off without even once looking at the children.
segments.summary: Gathering firewood, the girls find a dwarf with his beard trapped in a tree; despite his abuse they free him by cutting his beard, and he leaves ungrateful.

cohesion.time: Some time after the bear leaves
cohesion.place: The forest, by a felled tree

gacd.action: The girls pull at his beard, then Snow-white cuts it with scissors
gacd.conflict: Beard caught fast; the dwarf abuses and resists their help

segments.reason: Clear goal (help the dwarf), on-stage action (cutting the beard) meeting resistance (stuck beard, ungrateful dwarf), and interim outcome; unified forest setting, so dramatic_scene.

segments.start_exact: Some time afterwards Snow-white and Rose-red went to catch a dish of fish.
segments.end_exact:
he dragged it
      away and disappeared behind a stone.
segments.summary: At the brook the girls find the dwarf being pulled in by a fish tangled in his beard; they cut him free and he curses them, snatching a sack of pearls.

gacd.goal: Save the dwarf from being dragged into the water
gacd.action: They hold him and cut the entangled beard from the line
gacd.conflict: Beard and line entangled fast; the dwarf being pulled by the fish and then rages at them

segments.reason: New place (brook) and clear rescue action against resistance with an outcome; dramatic_scene.

segments.start_exact:
It happened that soon afterwards the mother sent the two children to the
      town
segments.end_exact:
gave
      the wicked creature a single blow with his paw, and he did not move again.
segments.summary: On a trip to town the girls rescue the dwarf from an eagle; later they surprise him with his jewels, and the bear arrives and kills the dwarf.

gacd.goal: Get through their errand / deal with the dwarf; ultimately the dwarf's fate
gacd.action: Girls pull the dwarf from the eagle; the bear attacks the dwarf
gacd.conflict: Eagle seizing the dwarf; dwarf's rage and betrayal; the bear confronts him

segments.reason: Unified by the heath setting across going and returning; sustained conflict (eagle, then bear) culminating in the dwarf's death, so dramatic_scene.

segments.start_exact: The girls had run away, but the bear called to them: \u\u
segments.end_exact:
every year bore the most beautiful roses,
      white and red.
segments.summary: The bear reveals he is a bewitched king's son freed by the dwarf's death; Snow-white and Rose-red marry him and his brother, living happily with their mother.

cohesion.place: The heath and later the family home

segments.reason: Resolution and happy-ending summary: revelation and marriages narrated without goal-conflict-outcome or deliberation structure, so narrative_scene.
